headline: The FBI and Google dismantled the two-million-device NetNut proxy network as artificial intelligence reshaped both offense and defense, pushing Apple to compress its patch cycles and letting Anthropic's Claude mine open-source code for thousands of flaws.

emerging_trends.text: Artificial intelligence now sets the tempo on both sides, as Anthropic's Claude Mythos surfaces thousands of open-source bugs and IBM assigns 20,000 engineers to fix them, while faster exploitation forces Apple to compress its patch cycles.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Turns Bug Hunter as Anthropic and IBM Scale Up

emerging_trends.text: Law enforcement and platform owners keep tearing down criminal infrastructure, with the FBI seizing hundreds of NetNut domains and Google degrading the two-million-device Popa botnet behind it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FBI and Google Dismantle NetNut Proxy Network

emerging_trends.text: Stolen edge-device credentials increasingly serve as the ransomware on-ramp, as FortiBleed operators monetize footholds in thousands of Fortinet firewalls and Anubis affiliates ride Citrix Bleed 2 into victim networks.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FortiBleed and Citrix Bleed 2 Feed Ransomware

topics.title: FortiBleed and Citrix Bleed 2 Feed Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported July 2 that FortiBleed operators began monetizing footholds in thousands of Fortinet firewalls and piled on a Nextcloud zero-day, with one operator working negotiation panels for both INC and Lynx, while The Hacker News tied Anubis affiliates to Citrix Bleed 2 (CVE-2025-5777) and Sophos linked the Vect and TeamPCP supply-chain credential theft to ransomware deployment.
topics.summary: FortiBleed harvested credentials from hundreds of thousands of FortiGate firewalls, and INC and Lynx affiliates are now converting that access into intrusions, joined by Anubis crews exploiting Citrix Bleed 2 for initial access. Rotate credentials on exposed edge appliances and hunt for remote-management tooling abuse.

sources.title: FortiBleed Actors Collaborating With Inc, Lynx Ransomware Gangs
Ransomware Groups Turn to Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD, and Supply Chain Credentials
Vect and TeamPCP partner for ransomware campaigns
FortiBleed Campaign Linked to INC, Lynx Ransomware Attacks

topics.title: AI Turns Bug Hunter as Anthropic and IBM Scale Up
topics.latest_developments: IBM and Red Hat assigned 20,000 engineers to a new Project Lightwell service to patch the flaws Anthropic's Claude Mythos surfaces, after the preview combed more than 23,000 open-source code paths and routed 1,596 verified vulnerabilities to maintainers, as the Trump administration lifted restrictions and Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.
topics.summary: Anthropic's Mythos preview finds open-source vulnerabilities at machine speed, swamping volunteer maintainers who already field more reports than they can act on. IBM's Project Lightwell aims to close that patch gap; CISOs need audit strategies for AI-generated code before it reaches production.

sources.title: Anthropic's AI Finds Bugs. IBM Bets $5B It Can Fix Them.
What the AI patch gap means for enterprise security
Trump Administration Lifts Restrictions on Anthropic's Claude Models After Cybersecurity Alarm

topics.title: FBI and Google Dismantle NetNut Proxy Network
topics.latest_developments: The FBI seized hundreds of NetNut domains July 2, two weeks after KrebsOnSecurity linked the service to the Popa botnet, while Google's Threat Intelligence Group, Lumen, and partners cut that two-million-device network's usable pool by millions.
topics.summary: NetNut, a residential-proxy service the publicly traded Israeli firm Alarum Technologies operates, rented roughly two million compromised home devices as traffic relays for other people's activity. Defenders should treat unexplained relay traffic from home routers and IoT gear as a compromise indicator.

sources.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
Google Disrupts NetNut Residential Proxy Network Spanning 2 Million Home Devices

topics.title: Cisco Confirms Unified CM Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Cisco confirmed July 2 that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-20230, a server-side request forgery flaw in Unified Communications Manager it patched in early June, with a public proof-of-concept available since disclosure and the first exploitation attempts observed last week.
topics.summary: The flaw lets attackers coerce Cisco's enterprise call-management server into issuing requests on their behalf, a foothold in voice infrastructure many organizations expose. Apply Cisco's June fix immediately and review server logs for anomalous outbound requests.

sources.title: Cisco finally confirms attackers exploiting Unified CM flaw
Cisco Confirms In-the-Wild Exploitation of Unified CM Vulnerability

topics.title: Europe Presses on Data Transfers and Google
topics.latest_developments: Max Schrems of the Vienna privacy group noyb told European officials in a July 1 letter he will sue to invalidate the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework after a U.S. Supreme Court decision, the same week the Court of Justice of the European Union dismissed Google's final appeal against a €4.1 billion antitrust fine over its use of Android to promote Chrome and search.
topics.summary: The Data Privacy Framework governs lawful transfer of Europeans' personal data to U.S. companies, and a successful noyb challenge would strand thousands of firms that rely on it. Companies moving EU data westward should track the litigation and prepare fallback transfer mechanisms.

sources.title: Supreme Court decision threatens EU-US data transfer agreement
Google loses final appeal to overturn €4.1 billion EU fine

topics.title: Apple Reverses Its Patch-Timing Policy
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported July 2 that Apple abandoned a long-standing policy and will ship more compressed patching cycles, citing attackers who use artificial intelligence to shorten the time between disclosure and working exploits.
topics.summary: Apple historically batched and paced its security fixes; the shift means faster, more frequent releases across iOS, macOS, and Safari. Enterprises should expect tighter update windows and adjust deployment testing accordingly.

sources.title: Apple Reverses Age-Old Patch Policy to Keep Up With AI

Valdez helps Pirates beat Phillies 6-1 to split their four-game series

business_politics.title: Russia Launches One of the War's Largest Barrages on Kyiv
business_politics.latest_developments: Russia struck Kyiv over several hours on July 2 with 74 missiles and nearly 500 drones, one of the war's largest single attacks, hours after Volodymyr Zelensky warned Moscow was preparing a massive strike.
business_politics.summary: Ballistic and cruise missiles and waves of drones hit Ukraine's capital, killing at least 21 people, as Zelensky presses a drone-war surge meant to force Moscow toward peace talks.

sources.title: Russia unleashes huge bombardment on Kyiv
Russia Pounds Ukraine's Capital in One of War's Largest Attacks

business_politics.title: US June Payrolls Undershoot at 57,000
business_politics.latest_developments: The United States added just 57,000 jobs in June, the Labor Department reported July 2, ending a three-month streak of overperformance and weakening the dollar broadly as markets pulled forward Federal Reserve rate-cut bets.
business_politics.summary: The sharp hiring slowdown missed forecasts and pushed the dollar down, easing pressure for a Japanese intervention to prop up the yen, though Treasury yields still finished the holiday-shortened week higher.

sources.title: US economy undershoots forecasts with 57,000 jobs added in June
Potential Yen-Supporting Intervention Expected to Have Limited Results

business.title: Alcoa Buys South32 Australian Assets for $4.1 Billion
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's Alcoa agreed July 2 to acquire South32's Australian aluminum assets in a $4.1 billion deal.
business.summary: Alcoa, the aluminum producer headquartered in Pittsburgh, is picking up South32's operations in Australia, expanding its bauxite and alumina footprint.

sources.title: Alcoa picks up Australian assets in $4.1 billion deal

business.title: 'Mayor of Kingstown' Wraps Final Season in Pittsburgh
business.latest_developments: The Paramount+ series 'Mayor of Kingstown' finished filming its fifth and final season in Pittsburgh, the Pittsburgh Film Office said July 2.
business.summary: Since 2022 the show shot 457 days across western Pennsylvania, injecting more than $325 million into the local economy and creating over 10,000 jobs, according to the Pittsburgh Film Office.

sources.title: "Mayor of Kingstown" wraps up filming final season in Pittsburgh

around_town.title: Allegheny County Faces $1.4 Billion Pension Shortfall
around_town.latest_developments: A consultant's report shows Allegheny County's pension fund is underfunded by $1.4 billion, and county leaders say taxpayers may have to cover the gap.
around_town.summary: The shortfall lands a year after a 36% property tax increase; county workers have paid into the plan expecting steady retirement income, and leaders remain unsure how to close the hole, KDKA reported.

sources.title: Allegheny County's pension fund crisis could leave taxpayers on the hook

around_town.title: I-376 to Close 25 Days for Commercial Street Bridge
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT will fully close a large stretch of I-376 from July 10 to August 3 to replace the Commercial Street Bridge near the Squirrel Hill Tunnel.
around_town.summary: The 25-day total closure of the Parkway East segment near Frick Park forces detours on one of the region's most heavily traveled routes, Pittsburgh Magazine reported.

sources.title: The Dreaded Closure of I-376 Is Coming. Here's What to Expect.

around_town.title: PennDOT Truck Spills 1,000 Gallons of Oil Into Mon Tributary
around_town.latest_developments: A PennDOT truck leaked about 1,000 gallons of oil into a Monongahela River tributary, and the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection opened an investigation.
around_town.summary: The spill contaminated a Pittsburgh-area tributary of the Monongahela; the DEP is investigating the source and extent, WPXI reported.

sources.title: PennDOT truck leaks 1K gallons of oil into Monongahela River tributary

events.title: Taste of Picklesburgh Previews the Festival Downtown
events.latest_developments: Taste of Picklesburgh runs Thursday, July 9, through Sunday, July 19, as a pickle-infused preview to the main Picklesburgh festival.
events.summary: Thirteen Downtown restaurants and one retailer across the Golden Triangle will serve pickle-inspired specials over the eleven days, Pittsburgh Magazine reported.

sources.title: It's a Big Dill: Jumpstart Pittsburgh's Fave Pickle Fest With a 'Taste of Picklesburgh'

events.title: Pittsburgh Marks America's 250th on the Fourth
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published a July 2 guide to America 250 celebrations across the Pittsburgh area, and WPXI Channel 11 confirmed it will broadcast the city's Independence Day fireworks on Saturday, July 4.
events.summary: Pittsburgh's Fourth of July festivities anchor the national semiquincentennial; residents can find events area-wide or watch the fireworks on WPXI.

sources.title: Here's where to celebrate America 250 in the Pittsburgh area
You can watch the Pittsburgh Independence Day fireworks on WPXI

around_teams.title: Hiles: Valdez Could Be the Bat Pirates Wanted in Ozuna
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles argued July 2 that rookie Esmerlyn Valdez can become everything the Pirates hoped Marcell Ozuna would be.
around_teams.summary: Valdez has homered in four straight games and drove in three during the Phillies series; Hiles frames the young designated hitter as the answer to Pittsburgh's disappointing Ozuna signing.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Esmerlyn Valdez can be everything the Pirates hoped Marcell Ozuna would be

around_teams.title: Marcus Freeman Joins Cam Heyward's 'Not Just Football'
around_teams.latest_developments: Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman sat down with Steelers captain Cam Heyward on the 'Not Just Football' podcast, posted July 1.
around_teams.summary: Freeman traced his path from Ohio State linebacker to Notre Dame head coach and talked leadership, recruiting, handling pressure, and developing NFL talent, alongside his friendship with Heyward.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: Marcus Freeman on Coaching Notre Dame, Being Teammates With Cam, And More! | Not Just Football

around_teams.title: Two Pirates Prospects Named to All-Star Futures Game
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates' Seth Hernandez and Edward Florentino earned selection to the 2026 MLB All-Star Futures Game, the Post-Gazette reported July 1.
around_teams.summary: Hernandez, the organization's top pitching prospect and the first minor leaguer to reach 100 strikeouts this season, joins outfielder Edward Florentino in the prospect showcase.

sources.title: The Pirates' Seth Hernandez, Edward Florentino have been selected to the All-Star Futures Game

team_usa.title: US Olympic Canoeist Indicted in Reflecting Pool Case
team_usa.latest_developments: A Washington grand jury indicted three-time US Olympic canoeist David Hearn on July 2 on a felony charge over damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
team_usa.summary: The indictment accuses Hearn of maliciously destroying lining material at the pool on June 19, following a $14.7 million renovation that left liner peeling; President Trump had called the incident vandalism.

sources.title: Ex-Olympian indicted in Reflecting Pool case

team_usa.title: USMNT Faces Belgium in Round of 16 Without Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN assessed July 2 how the United States can advance past Belgium in the World Cup round of 16 without suspended top scorer Folarin Balogun.
team_usa.summary: Belgium reached the last 16 by rallying from two goals down to beat Senegal in extra time; ESPN argues the US, having shown it can win ugly, has the tools to move on despite losing Balogun to a red card.

sources.title: USMNT shows it can play ugly, which is exactly what it needs

reading.title: The AI Industry Is Losing
reading.summary: Zitron argues the AI industry is losing, contending its economics and returns fail to justify the enormous capital pouring into companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and NVIDIA.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Beware of Productivity Paradoxes
reading.summary: Newport examines how technologies that seem poised for obvious productivity gains, like the personal computer, often fail to deliver them, and warns against assuming AI will prove different.
